title: On Remembering the way to the mill in the dark
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：remember　|　正文 385 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 remember 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the director ① remembered the way to the mill in the dark for the whole place, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② remembers the way to the mill in the dark without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ remember the way to the mill in the dark at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ remembered the way to the mill in the dark before — a line in the poster for August 1955 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Remembering the way to the mill in the dark for the whole place, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ remember the date without being told without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Remember the date without being told at once and never mention it again.

By 1968 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ remembers the date without being told for the whole place every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ remembered the way to the mill in the dark again when nobody else would.

⑩ To remember the way to the mill in the dark, my mother said in 1973, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody remembers the way to the mill in the dark without a word of thanks again and somebody must remember the way to the mill in the dark for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 记得（一般过去式 remembered the way to the mill in the dark：1961 年导演头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 记得（一般现在 remembers the way to the mill in the dark：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 记得（不定式 to remember the way to the mill in the dark：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 记得（过去完成时 had remembered the way to the mill in the dark：1955 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 记得（动名词 remembering the way to the mill in the dark 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 记住（remember the date without being told：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去记住不用提醒也记着那个日子）
G. v. 记住（remember the date without being told：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 记得（后段两处：新来的演员照例 remembers the date without being told，而母亲又一次 remembered the way to the mill in the dark）

answers.why: remember 意为“记得”，1961 年导演替所有人记得黑地里还记得去磨坊的路，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 remembered。
remember 意为“记得”，自那以后导演不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 remembers。
remember 意为“记得”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯记得黑地里还记得去磨坊的路”，此处为不定式 to remember the way to the mill in the dark。
remember 意为“记得”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1968 年之前就有人记得过，故用过去完成时 had remembered。
remember 意为“记得”，导演说“记得黑地里还记得去磨坊的路这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 remembering the way to the mill in the dark 作主语。
remember 意为“记住”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去记住不用提醒也记着那个日子”，should ever 之后用原形 remember the date without being told。
remember 意为“记住”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻记住不用提醒也记着那个日子（remember the date without being told at once），以后再也不要提起。
remember 意为“记得”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例记住不用提醒也记着那个日子，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 remembers。
remember 意为“记得”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人记得黑地里还记得去磨坊的路，用一般过去式 remembered 叙述。
remember 意为“记得”，结尾那句是母亲 1973 年的话：要记得黑地里还记得去磨坊的路，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 remember 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the director remembered the way to the mill in the dark for the whole place, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director remembers the way to the mill in the dark without a word of thanks whenever the theatre asks.
Remembering the way to the mill in the dark for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever remember the date without being told without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre remembers the date without being told for the whole place every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother remembered the way to the mill in the dark again, and the theatre remembered that half.
